Subject: Request: Reserved GPU guarantee variance for scheduled batch windows

Hi Monica,

Quick note from procurement at VectorCloud — we’re finalizing the Dedicated capacity purchase (VC-2026-077) and the procurement/legal teams flagged a potential mismatch between your standard reserved-GPU SLA and our nightly batch ingestion windows.

Operationally, we run heavy model scoring jobs daily from 00:30–03:30 PST and occasionally a larger monthly reindex overnight. During those windows we expect an order-of-magnitude increase in synchronous batch traffic that would otherwise push normal low-latency requests into the tail.

Before we sign, legal wants clarity on two items:
- Whether Redwood can provide a temporary SLA variance (guaranteed minimum throughput for interactive traffic) during pre-booked batch windows, and
- If Redwood will reserve burst capacity or allow pre-scheduled queue-priority so our customer-facing latency SLO (p95 < 200ms) is preserved.

Can you outline what options are available (exceptions, credits, pre-booked bursts) and any operational steps we need to take? We can share internal traffic profiles if that helps. Looping in procurement for visibility.

Thanks,

Sarah Ong
Director, Procurement — VectorCloud
procurement@vectorcloud.com

Subject: RE: Request: Reserved GPU guarantee variance for scheduled batch windows

Monica / Lauren —

I reviewed the VectorCloud description. Technically we have two workable approaches; both require pre-booking and a short lead time to configure routing:

1) Pre-booked burst pool + interactive carveout (recommended)
- Reserve a small burst pool (10–20% of their Dedicated pool) that is consumed only during scheduled windows.
- Configure router to enforce an interactive carveout: interactive routes (tagged) get served from a separate front-tier pool with guaranteed baseline throughput (e.g., 750 tokens/s) while batch jobs drain from burst nodes.
- Impact: minimal; interactive p95 preserved. Burst usage is metered and billed at higher unit rate or drawn from committed burst credits.

2) Queue-priority slices (softer guarantee)
- Assign priority slices in the queueing layer so interactive requests preempt batch work up to a configured concurrency.
- Impact: less deterministic for very large, simultaneous batch spikes; simpler to implement but requires careful headroom settings.

Telemetry / gating we need from VectorCloud:
- Typical p95 interactive token latency under baseline (current numbers)
- Expected token/sec during batch window peak and duration
- Whether monthly reindex windows can be pre-scheduled with a 48-hour notice

I attached a short metrics proposal that maps capacity tiers to expected interactive token throughput and suggested crediting language.

-Aditya

Aditya Rao
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Proposed SLA variance and operational playbook — VectorCloud Dedicated purchase (VC-2026-077)

Hi Sarah / Josh —

Thanks for the patience while we reviewed this internally. Attached is a short proposal and a draft amendment to the Dedicated SLA that reflects the pre-booked variance for nightly batch windows. Summary below.

Proposal (high level):
- Baseline guarantee: reserved GPUs provide interactive baseline throughput of 900 tokens/s (aggregated p95 target < 200ms for tagged interactive routes).
- Scheduled variance window: 00:30–03:30 PST daily (VectorCloud to confirm any exceptions). During this period:
  - Redwood will make available a pre-booked burst pool sized at 20% of the reserved capacity for batch work;
  - Interactive traffic will be protected by a carveout guaranteeing a minimum interactive throughput of 600 tokens/s;
  - If burst consumption exceeds the pre-booked pool, interactive traffic falls back to best-effort with prioritized queuing.
- Credits/remedies: if interactive p95 > 350ms for more than 3 hours in a calendar month during scheduled windows, VectorCloud will be eligible for a pro-rated service credit (draft language in attachment).
- Operational steps: VectorCloud provides weekly traffic samples and 48-hour notice for any exceptional monthly jobs; Redwood will provision burst nodes and update routing policies before the scheduled window.

Attachments: variance-metrics-proposal.pdf, redwood_sla_amendment_draft.docx (contains legal-friendly amendment text).

Next steps: please confirm the daily window and whether the monthly reindex needs an exception flow. If you’re comfortable, Lauren will convert the amendment draft into a formal addendum and we’ll schedule a 30-minute call to finalize.

Best,

Monica Patel
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
